epic.title: Veterinary Clinic Operating System
epic.description: Deepen the existing healthcare-wellness/veterinary-clinic leaf into a safe, role-specific operating system. The canonical Oak & Prairie scenario is the acceptance spine for MVP slices and also funds convergence of the shared archetype scenario substrate so later archetype tests reuse one declarative fixture across deterministic demos, simulation, live exercise, and audit.
epic.scopeRationale: The business capability scope is the existing veterinary-clinic leaf; its acceptance-fixture infrastructure is deliberately reusable across archetypes but is delivered as part of this veterinary deepening epic.

items.title: Author the Oak & Prairie Julia veterinary acceptance fixture
items.body:
## Problem
The design defines Oak & Prairie and Julia, but executable demo flavor still names Meadowbrook/Iris and the audit contains another clinic identity. The canonical journeys, roles, animals, resources, stock, policies, integrations, and failure states are not loadable as one fixture.

## Scope
Author the Oak & Prairie scenario from the approved design: Julia and staff, guardians and animals, rooms/equipment/kennels, appointments/urgent reserve, encounters/procedures, medication and lot stock, controlled and waste evidence, retail food, workforce call-out, lab/payment/distributor stubs, clocked exceptions, export/restore, and deterministic cleanup. Regulated facts remain evidence-labelled and reviewer-gated.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fixture covers every named golden journey in design §12 and minimum acceptance journey in §14 that belongs to the scenario slice.
- Julia, DVM, technician, CSR/manager, and client views have deterministic expected outcomes.
- Wrong-tenant/animal/guardian, insufficient role, duplicate/out-of-order, stock/temperature/recall, interruption, offline, and recovery cases are represented.
- Demo flavor and audit identity converge on Oak & Prairie; no parallel practice authority remains.
- Reset/reload produces the same state and export/restore reconciles.
- 20% refactoring allocation removes conflicting fixture identities and leaf-local helpers.

Blocked by: canonical scenario-contract BI. Blocks live role/job runner and rollout BI.

Parent: BI-79449954.

items.title: Canonical Oak & Prairie veterinary fixture and reusable archetype acceptance-scenario convergence
items.body:
## Problem

The approved veterinary design defines Oak & Prairie and Julia as the canonical acceptance scenario, but no executable plan or shared fixture contract connects that scenario to the deterministic Demo Business generator, business-activity simulator, live exercise harness, UX/job validation, and audit. Current definitions already conflict (Oak & Prairie/Julia in the design, Meadowbrook/Iris in demo flavor, and an older clinic identity in the audit), so further archetype tests would multiply drift.

## Scope

In scope:
- one validated declarative archetype acceptance-scenario overlay that extends the existing DemoBusiness substrate;
- adapters for deterministic demo projection, simulator flows, live HTTP exercise, persona/job UX checks, and audit reporting;
- the complete Oak & Prairie/Julia fixture with reset/replay, negative, safety, compliance, inventory, staffing, retail, export/restore, and mobile/desktop cases;
- lessons from the Pet Rescue dogfood cycle, including subject/resource generalization, archetype-aware vocabulary and WWWD starters, inventory, occupancy, care schedules, veterinary coordination, first-viewport relevance, and live fresh-install readiness;
- a tiered rollout model for all archetypes and an explicit 20% refactoring allocation to remove duplicate fixture authorities.

Out of scope:
- implementing the clinical, controlled-substance, or jurisdiction-specific product slices themselves;
- claiming legal or clinical correctness without the external reviewers required by the design;
- a parallel veterinary-only harness or duplicate business identity store.

## Acceptance criteria

- A committed plan maps every independently shippable deliverable to a live BI and carries a validated backlog-coverage receipt.
- Exactly one scenario definition owns business identity, roles, personas/subjects, resources, catalog, demand/events, stock, policies, integrations, clock, expected outcomes, UX oracles, and cleanup.
- Demo, simulator, live harness, audit, and future archetype tests consume projections/adapters from that definition rather than restating it.
- Oak & Prairie exercises Julia and all named staff/client journeys from the canonical design, including negative and recovery states.
- The plan specifies first-viewport, job-step, accessibility, mobile, compliance/safety, replay, teardown, export/restore, and cross-archetype regression evidence.
- Pet Rescue findings are traced to generalized fixture requirements or explicitly excluded with rationale.
- At least 20% of each implementation slice is reserved for fixture/substrate convergence and removal of superseded definitions.

## Dependencies

Blocked by regulated-slice promotion on the veterinary, technician, Illinois legal/compliance, controlled-substance/waste, security, and accessibility reviews named in the design. Fixture-framework implementation and non-clinical test data authoring may proceed before those reviews, but regulated assertions may not.

## Context

- Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-veterinary-clinic-operating-system-design.md`
- Existing demo plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-archetype-demo-factory-execution.md`
- Live exercise playbook: `docs/testing/archetype-exercise-playbook.md`
- Pet Rescue findings: `EP-5102F494`
- Architecture decision: `DI-BFA0999EA4C1` (extend Demo Business with a companion acceptance-scenario overlay).
items.scopeRationale: Oak & Prairie is the first deep fixture, while the scenario contract and adapters are shared test infrastructure for all archetypes.

items.title: Define the canonical archetype acceptance-scenario contract and DemoBusiness derivation
items.body:
## Problem
DemoBusiness supplies deterministic demo state, while simulator and live-harness scenarios carry separate behavior definitions. There is no validated companion contract for jobs, subjects, resources, events, expected outcomes, UX oracles, or cleanup.

## Scope
Define a typed, versioned acceptance-scenario overlay in @dpf/storefront-templates, derived from and linked to DemoBusiness. Include identity, clock, roles, personas/subjects, resources, catalog, demand/events, inventory, policy/applicability, integration stubs, expected outcomes, UX oracles, evidence labels, and cleanup. Reject duplicate business identity and nondeterministic clocks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Schema and validator reject duplicate identity, unknown references, unsupported capabilities, unsafe regulated claims, and nondeterminism.
- Every scenario references one archetype and one DemoBusiness authority.
- Unit/property/snapshot tests prove stable derivation and backward compatibility.
- 20% refactoring allocation is used to consolidate existing demo schema/helpers exposed by the change.

Blocked by: none. Blocks the adapter and Oak & Prairie fixture BIs.

Parent: BI-79449954.
items.scopeRationale: The contract is shared test substrate; veterinary-clinic is its first deep consumer.

items.title: Converge demo, simulator, live harness, and audit on scenario adapters
items.body:
## Problem
The Demo Business generator, business-activity simulator, live exercise harness, and archetype audit currently restate business behavior in incompatible shapes. The playbook already identifies this drift risk.

## Scope
Build thin projections from the canonical acceptance-scenario contract into deterministic demo load, simulator flows, live HTTP exercise, audit/job reports, and cleanup. Preserve each runner's purpose; do not create a new runner. Remove or redirect duplicate scenario definitions after parity proof.

## Acceptance criteria
- One source scenario produces all runner inputs.
- Restaurant remains behaviorally equivalent through a compatibility adapter.
- Load/unload is idempotent and source-tag isolated.
- Adapter contract tests cover reference integrity, unsupported steps, failures, and deterministic replay.
- Superseded duplicate definitions are removed only after snapshot and live parity evidence.
- At least 20% of the slice is explicit convergence/debt removal.

Blocked by: canonical scenario-contract BI. Blocks live Oak & Prairie execution and rollout BI.

Parent: BI-79449954.

items.title: Establish tiered archetype fixture CI, replay, and rollout governance
items.body:
## Problem
Running every deep live journey for every archetype is too costly, while shallow generation alone misses runtime, vocabulary, authority, and workflow failures. Counts and fixture identities have also drifted in documentation.

## Scope
Implement coverage tiers: deterministic contract tests for all archetypes; lightweight scenario-delta checks for all; category sentinel live tests; operational-twin shape tests; risk-selected deep fixtures; external domain validation for regulated leaves. Add replay, teardown, export/restore, evidence retention, dynamic catalog counts, and a learning register that routes durable findings to shared substrate/BIs.

## Acceptance criteria
- CI selects tiers by changed substrate, archetype risk, category, and operational shape.
- All current archetypes are enumerated dynamically; no hand-maintained counts.
- Every live run proves setup, execution, cleanup, replay, and finding capture.
- Pet Rescue lessons are represented as regression requirements, including subject/resource generalization, inventory, occupancy, scheduled care, veterinary coordination, archetype-aware vocabulary/stances, and first-viewport relevance.
- Runtime-heavy gates only run when their impact contract requires them.
- 20% refactoring allocation removes stale counts, duplicate docs, and runner-specific scenario rules.

Blocked by: scenario adapters and acceptance runner BIs. Parent: BI-79449954.
items.scopeRationale: Coverage tiers and rollout governance apply across the entire archetype catalog.

items.title: Add role, job, first-viewport, safety, and accessibility acceptance execution
items.body:
## Problem
Current live harness drives catalog demand but does not execute per-role jobs or prove that DPF reduces burden against a pre-DPF baseline. It also lacks systematic first-viewport, mobile, accessibility, safety, denial, and recovery assertions.

## Scope
Extend the existing live exercise path to authenticate seeded roles, execute scenario job steps, capture step/time/error baselines, assert first-viewport relevance and drill-through, check accessibility/mobile states, and record safety/compliance denials and recovery evidence. Use shared UX primitives and the canonical runtime/leased preview only.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each Julia/staff/client job records pre-DPF baseline, DPF step count, completion, errors, evidence, and unresolved findings.
- First viewport shows role-relevant urgent work without a duplicate dashboard.
- Desktop plus Julia/technician mobile widths, keyboard, screen-reader labels, focus, contrast, loading/empty/error/offline/denied states are tested.
- Unsafe prescribing/release/controlled actions fail closed and capture evidence.
- Findings automatically map to live BIs without mutating the tested fixture's authority.
- 20% refactoring allocation consolidates job/oracle/login helpers.

Blocked by: scenario adapters and Oak & Prairie fixture BIs. Blocks rollout BI.

Parent: BI-79449954.
